oh_baker_run.blurb: Baker Run is a small sandstone bouldering spot in the Marietta Unit of Wayne National Forest, roughly a quarter-hour drive from the town of Marietta. About two dozen problems are scattered over a couple of acres of hillside, and most are in the easy to moderate range: a good number of VB to V1 lines, a handful at V2 to V4, and just a few harder ones reaching into V5 and V6. Boulders stand around 10 to 15 feet tall and the styles run from slabs to steep overhangs. The slope catches sun late in the day. The boulders can be seen from the road, so the walk is short, which makes it an easy stop for a quick session.

oh_bell_ridge_boulders_climbs.blurb: Bell Ridge Boulders is a compact bouldering area in the Marietta Unit of Wayne National Forest in southeast Ohio. The blocks line a narrow climbers' path, so you meet them one after another within about half a mile of where you park. There are around two dozen problems, and the bulk fall between V2 and V4, with a few easier warm-ups and a handful of harder lines up to V5 and V6. It suits a relaxed half-day of moderate bouldering with a small group rather than a big destination trip, and a smaller sister cluster, Bell Ridge North, sits alongside it for a little extra variety.

oh_stone_church.blurb: Stone Church is a roadside bouldering area in Tri-Valley Wildlife Area, in the central part of the state near Zanesville. It holds a couple of dozen problems on sandstone blocks sitting a short way from the car, so setup is quick. Climbing leans friendly: plenty of VB to V2 problems for newer boulderers, a middle group around V3 and V4, and a small top end with several lines from V6 up to V8 for people looking to project. Mushroom-shaped blocks and slopey, technical moves are part of the flavor. It works well for a short visit when you want both easy circuits and a few serious challenges in one spot.

oh_middle_cliff_the.blurb: The Middle Cliff is a short sandstone wall in the former quarry at Logtown near Lisbon, in eastern Ohio, set downstream of the larger Big Cliffs. Most of the twenty-odd lines are trad, with a smaller group of bolted sport routes, covering everything from beginner-level 5.4 and 5.5 up to about 5.11, with the largest cluster in the 5.4 to 5.9 range. The stone is fine-grained and generally solid. The wall faces east and usually stays cool and shaded, which helps on warm days. The top is steep and littered with loose debris, so it works best as a lead-and-lower or lead-then-rig wall.
oh_middle_cliff_the.parking_note: Park in the lot off Logtown Road, short of the bridge where Lisbon ends, just past the point where the paved bike path crosses the road.
